objectives: Decode taught CVC words containing short /o/.
Blend three phonemes into a complete word.
Distinguish short /o/ from short /a/ and /i/ during decoding.
Correct inaccurate decoding by returning to grapheme-level analysis.
concepts: Systematic decoding proceeds from grapheme to phoneme to blended word.
The middle vowel is essential to CVC decoding.
Minimal contrasts help identify vowel decoding errors.

definitions.definition: Using written graphemes to identify the sounds in a word and blend them.
Combining individual phonemes to pronounce a word.
A simple consonant-vowel-consonant word such as hot or mop.

workedExamples: hot read as hat → return to o, say /o/, then blend again.
commonMistakes: Changing a consonant instead of checking the vowel.

basic: Decode hot, mop, pot and log.
conceptual: Identify the vowel causing a decoding error.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why hot and hat require attention to the middle vowel.
mixedReview: Decode short /o/ words and contrast with short /a/ and /i/.

formulaOrFactBank: short /o/ → o in taught CVC words
weakTopicRevision: Return to individual grapheme sounds before blending again.

outcomes: Learner decodes short /o/ CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner blends three phonemes into complete words.
Learner identifies short /o/ versus /a/ decoding errors.
Learner self-corrects inaccurate decoding using grapheme-level checking.
